note: Window agent p1720-p1729, 2 Nov 2026. Pages opened: Viceroyalty of New Granada, Tahmasp II, Campaigns of Nader Shah, Mahmud Hotak, Dzungar conquest of Tibet, Tibet under Qing rule, Hotak dynasty. keyframe_overrides/1, /2 and /3 replace keyframes whose spans run past 1729 (Safavid and Qing 1727-1733, Peru 1723-1738), so they also act in the next window.

region.text: Lhasa and Central Tibet, handed to the Ganden Phodrang under the Qing protectorate after the Dzungars' expulsion

events.note: 1720: 'In 1720, the Qing dynasty sent a large force under the leadership of Prince Xun, Yunti'; 'The larger expedition expelled the Dzungars and directly led to the Qing rule of Tibet'; after the liberation 'the Ganden Phodrang aligned themselves to the Qing authority'. The dzungar-khanate ledger/16 gives Central Tibet to the Qing outright in 1720 and the Tibet row only snaps to it in 1721 (tibet_1721: 4169 cells); the qing-dynasty ledger/35 books Tibet as a vassal from 1720, so the land is Tibet's, drawn in the Qing tint, from the end of 1720.

Shiraz
Kashan

correction.text: the Kandahar-Sistan lands of 1721 with Isfahan, Shiraz and Kashan, as in 1722-1726: Ashraf's holdings until he fled Isfahan in November 1729; without Khorasan, the north and the west

keyframe_overrides.why: Cliopatria's 1727 outline (the whole Iranian plateau, 1.92 M km2) swallows 3,523 cells that the Hotaki never held. Campaigns of Nader Shah: the siege of Mashhad 'gifted the capital of Khorasan to Tahmasp' (after Fathali Khan's execution of 10 October 1726), Nader 'liberated Isfahan' only after the battles of 1729-1730, so Isfahan stayed Afghan until November 1729; Mahmud Hotak: the Ottomans and Russians seized land and Qazvin rose against the Afghans in January 1723. The honest 1727-1729 Hotaki land is the 1722-1726 keyframe (hotaki-dynasty_1722), unchanged. Counter-evidence weighed: the Hotak dynasty page says only that 'For the next seven years until 1729, the Hotaks were the de facto rulers of most of Persia' and names no provinces; the dated, placed statements are the ones used.

minus.text: the Kandahar-Sistan-Kerman lands of 1721 with Isfahan, Shiraz and Kashan, the central Persia of Mahmud and Ashraf

correction.text: the Safavid court of Tahmasp II and Nader in 1727-1728: Cliopatria's 1727 Persian plateau outline (no Caspian provinces, no Ottoman west) without the Hotaki land of the 1722 keyframe (Kandahar, Sistan, Isfahan, Shiraz, Kashan); Khorasan with Mashhad is Tahmasp's

keyframe_overrides.why: The 148 km2 Cliopatria sliver (replaced by a 150 km circle at Qazvin) reduces the Safavid state to 73 cells in 1727-1728, while 3,975 cells in 1726 and 5,335 in 1729. Campaigns of Nader Shah: Nader and Tahmasp took Mashhad ('The results of the siege had gifted the capital of Khorasan to Tahmasp'), Tahmasp was at Astarabad, and Nader marched from Mashad on 4 May 1729; Tahmasp II page: 'By 1729, Tahmasp had control of most of the country'. The Safavid land of 1726 is carried through 1727-1728, minus the Hotaki land.

union.text: Cliopatria's Qing shape of 1727 without Tuva

the area of Kham east of the Dri River annexed to Sichuan (Cliopatria's 1702 and 1734 cuts together, clipped to Sichuan: the Qinghai part comes with the province below; 2 stray cells in Xizang, at Zayu and on the Bhutan border, left out)
Amdo, made the province of Qinghai in 1724

correction.text: Cliopatria's Qing shape of 1727 plus eastern Kham east of the Dri River (annexed to Sichuan in 1726-1727) and the whole province of Qinghai (made a province in 1724); without Tuva (the Qing took it only in 1758)

keyframe_overrides.why: Tibet under Qing rule: 'The Qing made the region of Amdo into the province of Qinghai in 1724' and eastern Kham 'was annexed to Sichuan in 1726-1727 through a treaty'. The ok keyframe lacks 223 Sichuan and 79 Qinghai cells that the Qing ledger (ledger/36, and tibet ledger/20 as the counterpart loss) gives it, so the 1727 snap throws about 300 cells of Garze and Qinghai to nobody for good (qing-dynasty_1727: 2 added, 304 removed). [Review p1720-p1729: the Kham piece is clipped to Sichuan; unclipped it gave the Qing 2 isolated direct cells inside Central Tibet (97.7 E 28.5 N and 89.7 E 28.2 N) that are not Kham east of the Dri.] [Seam sm-04, 2 Nov 2026: this entry is replaced by the corrected one: Cliopatria's 1727 shape also carries Tuva (563 cells), which the Tuva page gives to the Khotgoid and Zunghar Khanates until 'In 1758, Tuva came under the Qing dynasty'; the Tuva cut matches p1690-p1699 keyframe_overrides/1. The Kham and Qinghai additions are unchanged.]

correction.text: Spanish South America without Cuyo and the Santo Domingo states of Venezuela, with Maynas (the Peruvian Amazon of Loreto) that Peru took back with the rest of New Granada's land

keyframe_overrides.why: Viceroyalty of New Granada page: suppressed 5 November 1723; 'Province of Maynas, 1717 to 1723 and 1739 to 1802', so Maynas lay outside New Granada in 1723-1739, which leaves it to Peru as the Peru ledger/2 says. The 1717 keyframes add Loreto explicitly; Cliopatria's Spanish Empire 1723 shape does not reach the Amazon, so this keyframe dropped 1,301 Loreto cells from Peru for good (viceroyalty-of-peru_1723: 0 added, 1,301 removed, kept by none) after New Granada held them to 1722.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1721 shape without Tuva (Tannu Uriankhai), which the Qing took only in 1758

keyframe_overrides.why: Seam sm-04, from p1690-p1699 keyframe_overrides/1. Tuva page: 'Khotgoid Khanate and Zunghar Khanate (1634-1758)' held Tuva and 'In 1758, Tuva came under the Qing dynasty'. The Qing keyframes of 1696-1757 carry Tuva (571 cells of the 1696-1705 shapes, 563 of the later ones). p1690-p1699 keyframe_overrides/1 already cuts it from the 1696 shape; without this entry the 1700 snap hands it back to the Qing. Tuva stays nobody's, as there.

correction.text: the dossier's own correction for this shape, plus Kamchatka

keyframe_overrides.why: Seam sm-04, from the p1710-p1719 and p1720-p1729 review: the Cliopatria shapes of the Russian Empire for 1721-1731 carry only 252 of Kamchatka's 1,731 cells (the 1734 shape has 1,711), so each snap, and the Tsardom's dissolution in November 1721, releases about 1,479 cells to nobody for 1721-1731 although the Tsardom's 1702-1718 overrides (p1700-p1709 keyframe_overrides/0-3, p1710-p1719 keyframe_overrides/2-4) keep them Russian. The Russian conquest of Siberia page: '1697-1698 - The annexation of Kamchatka by the expedition of Vladimir Atlasov' and 'In Kamchatka, the Russians crushed the Itelmen uprisings against their rule in 1706, 1731, and 1741'. The correction is the dossier's own with Kamchatka added. Not in this window: the 1732-1733 keyframe russian-empire_1732 has the same gap (p1730-p1739). [Review sm-04, 3 Nov 2026: the region Kamchatka (admin-1 Kamchatka Krai, 1,731 cells) also holds the 7 cells of the Commander Islands, which Cliopatria's 1734 shape lacks too; the Commander Islands page: Bering's ship 'wrecked on the otherwise uninhabited Bering Island' in 1741. They are cut (110 km round 55.0 N 166.4 E: those 7 cells only; 1,724 left).]
